description: At an apartment complex, hotel/motel or housing project, the property manager controls hot water temperature. What to ask to protect your child.
shortAnswer: The temperature of the hot water that comes out the spigot is controlled by the property manager. It's not a bad idea to ask the property manager what their policy is about how hot the water should be that gets delivered to tenants and guests (it better be 120 degrees Fahrenheit or less).

faq.q: What should parents ask a property manager about hot water safety?
faq.a: Ask how they enforce their hot water policy: who checks the thermostats in the boiler/hot water room? How often? Is the boiler room locked and off limits to other tenants/guests? Does your unit have installed an anti-scald device or mixing valve that would prevent excessively hot water from making it to your child?

faq.q: Where can a child with severe scald burns be treated in the Southeast?
faq.a: If your child already has scald burns and those burns are severe, you might want to consider taking your child to Children's Hospital of Alabama. They have the only pediatric burn center in the Southeast.

faq.q: Are property managers trained to prevent scald burns?
faq.a: Scald burn prevention ought to be a mandatory part of every property manager's training. Unfortunately it is not and at times this means innocent children suffer.
